title: Playing the Bienville Roof Sunday dances
summary: Dejan recalls Sunday evening dances on the Bienville Hotel roof in the 1920s, and a furniture-store owner who hired the band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: On the way downtown we passed near Lee Circle and you mentioned about the Bienville.
Yeah well we used to play there, oh well at that time I'm trying to figure I think. Was it a hotel then?

The Bienville Hotel. I think Stanley was playing piano. It was Billy's sister if I'm not mistaken, Bill Phillips and my brother and myself and Ruben McClendon was playing a banjo. We'll get him one night. I don't know where he lived. But he was playing banjo and he could play piano pretty good too. And we'd split every Sunday evening.
You say the Bienville Roof, did you play up on the roof? Yeah it was the Bienville Roof.
Right on the roof. What was it like?
Because now it's an office memory or something like that.
Well it was closed in but I mean you could go right to the wind and look all the way. It was a very fine dance place. It was one of the swankiest dance places you know.
As far dancing most of the day.
Yeah yeah beautiful bandstand, beautiful dance flow.
It wasn't just the place you played for dinner music or anything like that. No.
Regular dance. Yeah people hired band to dance and run the place you know for different occasions. It's like they do in the Tulane Room or one of them places you know. Very very fine place.
But when was that? Do you know?
Oh that was in the 20s. In the 20s? Yeah that was in the 20s. That was in the 20s.
There was one band, Sharky played with them, Monk Hazel was the leader on a record date, Monk Hazel's band and his Bienville Roof band. Do you know if they were, that was in the 20s or something.

Yeah they must have been the house band I guess. Yeah maybe. Yeah. Because we just played on Sunday evening and I think the fella had a furniture store on the Royal Neal Canal. He was the one we was playing for the furniture store still there. I don't remember the name and I was nervous the same people have it. Yeah. You know the first furniture store you get coming from Canal Street on Royal Street? Well he's the one who used to hide a band to play up there. I remember I used to go to his place.
Isn't that what they call a Parisian room?
No it'd be across from there I think.
No right opposite the Parisian room, that's right, right opposite.
